newsitem.title: UK: Reed extends rally on database hopes.
newsitem.headline: Reed extends rally on database hopes.

text.p: Shares in Reed International Plc extended last month's sharp rebound on Friday as a report in the Financial Times renewed hopes for the publishing group's planned world scientific database.
Analysts said there was nothing new in the FT report but said the development of the database should be a long-term positive for Reed.

The stock, which plummeted to a nine-month intraday low of 10.25 stg in December in the wake of a poorly-received meeting with analysts, was up 11-1/2p at 11.01-1/2 stg by 1309 GMT. Trading volume reached a modest 499,379 shares.

"The FT report contains exactly what was said at last month's briefing, all the information was given out at that meeting except perhaps the cost of between 15 million stg and 18 million," said Mark Beilby, analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Anyway, Reed first announced its plan to set up comprehensive database to provide access to scientific literature in a press release dated August 1 1996.

It said ScienceDirect would feature an integrated database providing Internet access to the full text of all 1,200 Ellsevier science journals and the full text of other publishers who participated in setting up the database.
Reed said last August that the first release of the database, giving access to over 300 titles, would be tested in the first quarter of 1997.
Beilby said that the development of the database had helped allay fears that publishers such as Reed could be sidelined by new Internet distributors in a process known as "disintermediation."
"The point is that this shows it is not going to happen," Beilby said. "Reed has the huge back catalogue and a strong brand name and this is a very positive development."
He pointed out that Reed shares had rallied sharply from their tumble early last month. "That probably tells you they were oversold," he said. -- David Holmes, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
